newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ First-National end long talks session.
newsitem.headline: NZ First-National end long talks session.

text.p: New Zealand First and the National Party on Wednesday ended the longest session of coalition talks they have had so far with Prime Minister Jim Bolger describing them as "good".
"It was a good meeting," Bolger told reporters after the three hour, 10 minute meeting.
"They were long talks. They were good talks. We put a lot of energy into a lot of the detail work. There is a lot of work to be done to see whether we can bring it together."
Asked if the issue of superannuation was discussed, Bolger said: "A whole range of subjects were discussed, we did cover a lot of subjects today. It was included but not in detail."
Asked if there was room for compromise, he said National was taking an "across the board" approach looking at the issues.
New Zealand First is due to have a new session of talks with the Labour Party this afternoon.
The parties are in talks after the inconclusive election a month ago. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 4734 746
